def is_palindrome(text: str) -> bool:
    """
    Checks if given string is a palindrome.
    
    A palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards, ignoring case 
    (if desired; here we treat it as-is unless specified). This version
    checks exactly whether text == reversed(text), so uppercase/lowercase
    differences matter.

    >>> is_palindrome('')
    True
    >>> is_palindrome('aba')
    True
    >>> is_palindrome('aaaaa')
    True
    >>> is_palindrome('zbcd')
    False
    """
    return text == text[::-1]


# If you want to ignore case and non-alphanumeric characters:
def is_palindrome_ignore_case_and_non_alpha(text: str) -> bool:
    cleaned = ''.join(ch.lower() for ch in text if ch.isalnum())
    return cleaned == cleaned[::-1]

# Example usage:
if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(is_palindrome(''))          # True
    print(is_palindrome('aba'))       # True
    print(is_palindrome('aaaaa'))     # True
    print(is_palindrome('zbcd'))      # False
    
    # With case-insensitive version:
    print(is_palindrome_ignore_case_and_non_alpha("A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"))  # True
